subject: Proxy safelist audit + egress justification for private connectors
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.g@cedarcloud.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: CedarCloud Security <security@cedarcloud.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: minimal safelist + justification for private connectors

Hi Vivek,

As part of our private deployment onboarding checklist we need: 1) a minimal set of IPs/FQDNs and ports to allow from our private VPC so traffic to Redwood's private connectors won't be blocked, and 2) a short justification of why each destination is required (telemetry, model updates, licensing, health checks, etc.).

Also confirm whether Redwood supports routing outbound traffic through our customer proxy (with TLS passthrough) and whether SNI or TLS inspection breaks any model-update or package-download flows. Our security team has asked for an artefact we can attach to SEC-1223.

Can you send a concise manifest and any evidence (docs or signed MOA) we can include?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Manager, Cloud Security
CedarCloud

[Attachment: onboarding-checklist.csv]

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.g@cedarcloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimal safelist + justification for private connectors

On Sun, Jun 15, 2025 at 9:12 AM Samir Gupta <samir.g@cedarcloud.com> wrote:
> As part of our private deployment onboarding checklist we need: 1) a minimal set of IPs/FQDNs and ports to allow from our private VPC so traffic to Redwood's private connectors won't be blocked, and 2) a short justification of why each destination is required (telemetry, model updates, licensing, health checks, etc.).
> Also confirm whether Redwood supports routing outbound traffic through our customer proxy (with TLS passthrough) and whether SNI or TLS inspection breaks any model-update or package-download flows.

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask. Summary below plus attached CSV manifest (safelist_manifest.csv) and a short architecture note (redwood-egress-architecture.pdf).

Minimal safelist (explainers):
- 34.210.112.45, TCP 443 — control-plane API (heartbeat, policy checks). Required for rollout metadata and canary control.
- update-models.redwood-inference.com (CNAME -> s3/cdn), TCP 443 — model artifact downloads (periodic; resumable). If TLS is intercepted, downloads will fail unless certificate pinning/tunnel is preserved.
- telemetry-ingest.redwood-inference.com, TCP 443 (443 outbound) — aggregated anonymized latency/cost metrics (only from control-plane instances; payloads are non-PII). Optional if routing through your proxy is preferred.
- license-ops.redwood-inference.com, TCP 443 — license and entitlement validation (low QPS).
- time-sync NTP pools (pool.ntp.org), UDP 123 — time sync for cert validity checks (we can provide a fallback if blocked).

Proxy support and TLS inspection impact:
- We support routing via customer HTTP(S) proxies (explicit proxy config). For TLS inspection: if the proxy performs active MITM with custom root CA, model artifact downloads may fail if binaries are signed and we validate signatures during install. The recommended approach is TLS passthrough for update-models.* and telemetry.* endpoints, or allow the domains through the proxy without interception (SNI allowlist).

Firewall rule recommendations (customer side):
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to the listed FQDNs and the static IPs in the CSV.
- Permit outbound UDP/123 to NTP or use internal NTP mirror.
- Restrict inbound from Redwood (none required for private connectors; we initiate outbound).

Operational notes and controls:
- IPs in the manifest are region-scoped and marked ephemeral. We publish a 30-day rolling window of changes; recommend allowing by FQDN + proof-of-possession (mutual TLS) where possible.
- We provide a signed Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) attesting to minimal data egress categories and retention (attached: signed-moa.pdf).

Attachments: safelist_manifest.csv (IP/FQDN + port + TTL), redwood-egress-architecture.pdf (diagram + fallback options), signed-moa.pdf (governance).

If you'd like, we can produce a short audit bundle (logs showing previous model downloads + hashes) for SEC-1223 — Marissa can help pull that.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head, Partnerships (Redwood Inference)
T: +1 415-555-0189

[Attachment: safelist_manifest.csv] [Attachment: redwood-egress-architecture.pdf] [Attachment: signed-moa.pdf]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-17T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimal safelist + justification for private connectors

Hi Samir — quick follow-up from the compliance side. A couple of items we should add to SEC-1223 to expedite approval:

1) Ephemeral IP rotation evidence: I can attach a CSV export showing the last 90 days of egress IP changes for the region you're onboarding (we rotate some pool addresses when scaling).
2) Hashes and signed manifest: We should include a short script and an example of published artifact hashes (so you can verify model downloads even if TLS interception occurs).
3) Optional: if CedarCloud requires all telemetry proxied through their SIEM, we can provide a webhook and signed envelope so you get delivery receipts without decoding payloads.

Can you confirm whether you need NTP opened or whether you have an internal time source? If you prefer no UDP, we can package timestamp assertions with each TLS handshake for short-lived cert validation.

Next steps: if Samir confirms we will add the IP-rotation CSV to the evidence pack and send a small verification script. Targeting EOD Thursday (2025-06-19) for delivery.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance Enablement, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-06-18T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: minimal safelist + justification for private connectors

Samir —

Thanks for the patience. Confirming Redwood will provide:
- A signed safelist_manifest.csv (attached) with per-entry TTLs and the current region pool.
- Ephemeral-IP-change.csv (90 days) + example verification script (sha256 of published artifacts).
- A short note on TLS inspection implications and recommendations (we recommend SNI passthrough for update endpoints).
- A minimal MOA we can sign and return (attached signed-moa.pdf).

Action items for CedarCloud:
- Please decide whether you want model artifact traffic to be TLS-passthrough or proxied (with your proxy providing a CA). Our preference is TLS passthrough for update-models.* to preserve integrity checks.
- Confirm if you will allow the listed FQDNs by DNS name; if not we will supply a limited IP list but note it may change with scaling.

If you confirm proxy mode vs passthrough today we can finalize the evidence pack and attach to SEC-1223. I will escalate delivery if you need an internal sign-off earlier than 2025-06-19.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
